attempted_claim: Prove or disprove the following quantified fellow-traveling rigidity statement: fix c=1.3, C=1.6 with C < c^2, epsilon=0.05 and L=20 measured in the symmetrized Lipschitz metric on rank-5 Outer space CV5; let phi, psi in Out(F5) be primitive root-free atoroidal fully irreducible elements with stretch factors lambda_phi, lambda_psi in [c,C], each equipped with a periodic train-track folding axis L_phi, L_psi; if L_phi and L_psi contain oriented segments of symmetrized length at least L that epsilon-fellow-travel (pointwise symmetrized distance at most epsilon after orientation-preserving reparametrization) with the overlap certified by an explicit common sequence of consecutive Stallings folds with computed lengths, then phi is conjugate in Out(F5) to psi or psi^{-1}; a complete answer is either a proof of this implication for the fixed numerical parameters, or an explicit counterexample pair of certified primitive root-free atoroidal train-track representatives with stretch factors in [c,C], computed fellow-traveling segments meeting the length and epsilon bounds, and a rigorous non-conjugacy certificate via distinct stretch minimal polynomials, Whitehead data, or attracting-lamination invariants that is not a proper-power pair.
decisive_failure: The proof attempt stalled on a single explicit uniform estimate: a rigorous bound on symmetrized periods (inverse stretches, or a thick-part quasi-symmetry constant) for rank-5 primitive root-free atoroidal fully irreducible automorphisms with forward stretch in [1.3,1.6]. Script-verified margins (period counts, entry bound m<=281, power exclusion) and the precise gap analysis are recorded in WORKLOG.md, but no complete or disproving resolution of the admitted claim was established.
